text:
Detroit arrives at Calgary on the third game of a four-game road trip, riding points in six straight (3-0-3) after a 5-2 win at Vancouver two days ago. The Red Wings are without Mason Appleton and Marco Kasper. The Flames are home for the third game of a four-game stand, fresh off a 2-1 win over Minnesota, and are missing Samuel Honzek. Mikael Backlund could return; he's off the out list and day-to-day.

The numbers favor the visitors, though not by much. Our model projects 3.31 goals for DET and 2.77 for CGY. At five on five, Detroit has taken 52% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) and Calgary 48%. The Flames are better than their record, with a -19 goal difference against -4.2 expected, because finishing and goaltending have cost them. Detroit's power play (0.92 expected goals a game) outpaces Calgary's (0.45), and the Flames take 4.7 penalties a game.

In net, projected starters John Gibson (DET) and Dustin Wolf (CGY) are both below expectation this season, at -1.8 and -8.0 goals saved above expected. Gibson was 10.1 above last year; Wolf was -2.8. For Detroit, Alex DeBrincat (41% to score) leads the watch list. For Calgary, Matt Coronato is 53% for a point. Our under-the-radar pick is Michael Brandsegg-Nygård, with a dangerous shot profile lately and a 41% chance at a point.
